strengths: Novel and well-motivated architectural idea: adapting Mechanistic Neural Networks to snapshot single-cell data by predicting a locally-linear, state-conditioned ODE operator that admits a closed-form (matrix exponential) solution, avoiding numerical ODE solvers and OT preprocessing.

The projection of the latent linear operator back into gene-expression space yields directly interpretable pairwise gene interaction weights, a genuine advantage over black-box NODE/flow-matching baselines that only output velocities.

Strong and fairly comprehensive empirical evaluation: best average EMD across three standard benchmarks (Cite/EB/Multi) against many strong baselines (OT-MFM, OT-CFM, DeepRUOT, etc.), plus dedicated scalability (250K-cell inflation) and amortized/joint-training experiments that convincingly demonstrate the claimed benefits of removing OT preprocessing and enabling single-stage end-to-end training.

Biological validation against TRRUST database with an unsupervised activating/repressing classification task, including an ablation (fixing one eigenvalue to zero) that shows a sensible inductive-bias trade-off between predictive performance and interpretability.

Good engineering details (eigen-decomposition parametrization, invertibility regularizer, kinetic energy regularizer, complexity analysis) and reasonably thorough appendix with hyperparameters, proofs, and extensive qualitative UMAP visualizations aiding reproducibility.
weaknesses: The core comparison in Table 1 has notable gaps: several strong recent baselines (e.g., OT-MFM, DeepRUOT) are close in average performance, and Cell-MNN actually loses to OT-MFM on Cite and to OT-Interpolate is beaten only narrowly on some datasets; the margin of improvement is fairly modest given the added architectural complexity, and no statistical significance testing is reported despite reporting std over only left-out time points (not seeds combined with folds clearly).

TRRUST validation is limited to only 6 source genes with sufficient overlap, and F1 scores (50-80%) are only moderately above a 50% "guessing" baseline in Figure 4c; this is a fairly weak and small-scale form of biological validation for a paper's central novelty claim about interpretability, and no comparison to dedicated GRN-discovery baselines (e.g., PerturbODE, GRNBoost2) is provided on the same benchmark.

The 5-dimensional PCA latent space is quite small; it is unclear how much true gene-level biological complexity can be captured/attributed at this compression, and the paper's own limitation section acknowledges cubic scaling in latent dimension without any experiments at larger dz to demonstrate the tradeoff or validate that 5D is sufficient beyond prior heuristic practice.

The claim that the local linear ODE approximation remains valid over the observed prediction horizons is asserted only empirically ("we did not encounter this issue") without deeper analysis of when/why the linearization breaks down, which is a fairly important soundness caveat for a method whose core selling point is trustworthy mechanistic/explicit dynamics.

Some presentation issues: Table 1 has an apparent typo ("0,872" for I-CFM EB value), the amortization experiment description is a bit unclear about how cross-dataset PCA embeddings are merged given differing gene sets, and the paper doesn't discuss compute/wall-clock comparisons against baselines in the main results table despite scalability being a major claimed contribution.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated adaptation of Mechanistic Neural Networks to the single-cell snapshot setting, replacing black-box velocity prediction (as in Neural ODEs/Flow Matching) with an explicit, locally linear ODE operator that is interpretable in gene expression space.
Eliminates the OT preprocessing bottleneck used by SOTA methods (OT-MFM, DeepRUOT, OT-CFM), yielding a genuinely single-stage, end-to-end training pipeline.
Strong empirical results: best average EMD across three standard benchmarks (Cite, EB, Multi), and the only method to consistently beat the OT-Interpolate baseline on all three datasets.

Clear demonstrated advantage in scalability: baselines relying on Sinkhorn-based OT preprocessing hit OOM errors on inflated (250K-cell) datasets, while Cell-MNN and I-CFM continue to train, with Cell-MNN achieving the best MMD scores.

Amortized/joint training experiment across Cite and Multi shows Cell-MNN outperforms OT-CFM/I-CFM baselines, supporting the claim of easier foundation-model-style training due to the single-stage design.

Interpretability is not just claimed but quantitatively validated against the TRRUST literature-curated database via an unsupervised activating/repressing classification task, with a sensible ablation (fixing one eigenvalue to zero) showing a meaningful trade-off between predictive accuracy and interpretability.
Reasonable theoretical grounding (Proposition 1) justifying the local linear reparametrization of the dynamics, and clear complexity analysis relative to prior MNN variants.
Good related-work positioning distinguishing the work from NeuralODE-based, OT/flow-matching-based, and static GRN discovery methods.
weaknesses: The gene interaction discovery evaluation is based on very few source genes (6 genes with >10 TRRUST matches), and the reported F1 scores show large variance across seeds (e.g., 46%±33% for HMGA1 without the eigenvalue constraint), limiting confidence in the robustness of the interpretability claims.

All experiments use a fixed 5D PCA latent space; because gene interaction weights are derived by projecting the latent operator back through PCA loadings, the 'gene-level' interactions are indirectly inferred from a low-rank subspace, and the paper does not explore how sensitive conclusions are to this dimensionality choice or to alternative embeddings.
DeepRUOT baseline was rerun by the authors with modified preprocessing to match other methods, raising a minor concern about comparability/fairness versus the originally reported numbers.

No explicit empirical comparison against dedicated GRN-discovery baselines (e.g., PerturbODE, GRNBoost2, information-theoretic methods) on the same interaction-recovery task, only qualitative discussion in related work.

The core assumption of local linearity and single-step re-encoding could be more thoroughly stress-tested; the paper acknowledges the risk of leaving the valid regime for large Δt but states this was 'not encountered,' without a systematic experiment probing this limitation.

Confidence intervals for the main interpolation benchmark (Table 1) overlap between Cell-MNN and the next-best method (OT-MFM) on the Cite dataset, and no statistical significance testing is reported, making the 'best average performance' claim somewhat sensitive to variance.
The cubic-in-latent-dimension complexity is acknowledged as a limitation but not empirically explored beyond the fixed 5D setting, leaving scalability to richer latent spaces largely speculative.
